findings.summary: crates/server/src/board.rs:59: no test checks that a card's gate can come from its PR's branch records. When gates::latest(issue.gates.iter().chain(pr...gate)) is changed to gates::latest(issue.gates.iter()), all 4 github tests and both needs_you tests still pass. a_card_shows_the_latest_gate_from_its_comments_or_its_branch_and_its_pr never has a card whose gate comes from the branch: TRU-6's comment beats the branch record, and TRU-8's PR has no records. The behaviour does work end to end (TRU-6 showed Adversarial review round 1 from its records once its comments were removed).

Verification environment: the egress proxy adds a GitHub credential to requests to api.github.com. A curl with no token got X-RateLimit-Limit 15000. The server sent no Authorization header in this session (the proxy log shows auth=no on every request), but its reads upstream were authenticated by the proxy. So how the server behaves under GitHub's real 60-requests-an-hour anonymous limit was not observed. The repo that doesn't exist came back 403 from the proxy, not GitHub's 404.

No sdlc-board PR exists yet for TRU-10 (sdlc-board has no open PRs), so the end-to-end check used booking PR #53 served as open, plus a made-up pending PR, through the GitHub proxy. Real Linear tickets had their Stage labels overridden through the Linear proxy for TRU-6, TRU-7 and TRU-11 to TRU-13. Everything else was real data.
